description:
## Why

The first foundation piece for PKIX-baac. Every other child depends on being able to parse an SCT from bytes.

## What

Parse a single `SignedCertificateTimestamp` (RFC 6962 §3.2) and a `SignedCertificateTimestampList` wrapper (RFC 6962 §3.3) from bytes.

**SCT binary layout** (RFC 6962 §3.2, network byte order):

```
struct {
    Version sct_version;          // 1 byte; v1 = 0
    LogID id;                     // 32 bytes (SHA-256 of log pubkey DER)
    uint64 timestamp;             // 8 bytes (ms since Unix epoch)
    CtExtensions extensions;      // u16 length-prefixed bytes
    digitally-signed struct {     // signed_struct = TBS-context bytes
        HashAlgorithm hash;       // 1 byte (RFC 5246 §7.4.1.4.1)
        SignatureAlgorithm sig;   // 1 byte
        opaque signature<0..2^16-1>;  // u16 length-prefixed
    } signature;
} SignedCertificateTimestamp;
```

**SCT-list wrapper** (RFC 6962 §3.3): `opaque SerializedSCT<1..2^16-1>; SignedCertificateTimestampList { SerializedSCT sct_list<1..2^16-1>; }`. Outer u16 total length, then a sequence of u16-length-prefixed SCTs. When embedded in a cert extension, the extension value is itself an OCTET STRING containing the list.

## Public API

```rust
pub struct SignedCertificateTimestamp {
    pub version: u8,                  // 0 for v1
    pub log_id: [u8; 32],
    pub timestamp_ms: u64,
    pub extensions: Vec<u8>,          // usually empty for embedded SCTs
    pub hash_alg: u8,                 // RFC 5246 HashAlgorithm
    pub sig_alg: u8,                  // RFC 5246 SignatureAlgorithm
    pub signature: Vec<u8>,           // raw signature bytes
}

impl SignedCertificateTimestamp {
    pub fn from_bytes(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, Error>;
}

pub struct SctList(pub Vec<SignedCertificateTimestamp>);

impl SctList {
    /// Parse the extension value of OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.11129.2.4.2.
    /// Accepts either the raw SerializedSCTList bytes OR the DER OCTET STRING wrapping.
    pub fn from_extension_value(ext_value: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, Error>;
}
```

The existing `SignedCertificateTimestamp` skeleton in lib.rs needs the missing fields added (extensions, hash_alg, sig_alg, signature).

## Test fixtures + oracle

Independent oracle: pyca/cryptography's `cryptography.x509.certificate_transparency.SignedCertificateTimestamp` parsing, or `openssl x509 -text` pretty-printing of the SCT list extension.

Get a test cert: any current TLS cert with embedded SCTs. `openssl s_client -connect badssl.com:443 -showcerts < /dev/null | openssl x509 -outform DER > pkix-ct/tests/fixtures/cert-with-scts.der` works. Or grab from the workspace's existing test fixtures if any have SCTs.

Compute expected parsed values via openssl/pyca, hardcode as `hex!(...)` or committed test JSON.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `from_bytes` parses a single SCT.
- [ ] `from_extension_value` parses the cert-extension list shape (with DER OCTET STRING unwrap).
- [ ] At least 3 negative-test inputs (truncated SCT, bad length prefix, version != 0) reject cleanly.
- [ ] At least one real-world cert from a CT-required deployment parses cleanly.
- [ ] Test vectors come from openssl/pyca, NOT from this crate's own parsing.
- [ ] Crate-level `#![no_std]` introduced if not already (use `alloc::vec::Vec`).

## Effort

~150 lines + tests. ~half a day.

## Filed as

Child .1 of PKIX-baac per its recommended decomposition.
title: pkix-ct: SCT binary-format parser (RFC 6962 §3.2/§3.3)
